Apple today updated its vintage and obsolete product list, with the iPhone X and 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro now classified as obsolete. What does this mean?

iPhone X and 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro are now obsolete

Apple today updated its support article on "How to get service for your Apple products after the warranty period has expired," moving the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro and iPhone X from the vintage list to the obsolete list.

Apple has explained that once a product is added to the obsolete list, the company will discontinue all hardware repair services and service providers will no longer be able to order related parts.

Products may be classified as obsolete more than seven years after Apple stops selling them, but the actual timing of the classification is always at Apple's discretion.

On the other hand, Apple's vintage list includes products that will continue to receive repairs only while parts remain in stock. Apple considers products obsolete that have been off sale for more than five years but less than seven years.

Apple dropped major OS support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, with iOS 16 being its last major version. The device now only supports up to iOS 16.7.16. As for the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro, it only supports up to macOS Sequoia and can now be updated to macOS 15.7.7.
